panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Panel A is a gross specimen of an excised duct from a patient with periductal mastitis, showing a dilated duct with thick secretions; the disease attribution is supported by the disease-focused article and in-text confirmation of periductal mastitis. B: Panel B is an H&E histology image of breast tissue showing a dilated central duct with thick secretions and a surrounding cuff of chronic periductal inflammation, the classic histopathologic manifestation of periductal mastitis.

panels.rationale: Single clinical photograph of a real patient showing a right subareolar inflammatory mass/abscess in periductal mastitis, with aspiration of thick pus as described in the caption and text. The disease attribution is directly supported by the caption and article focus.
panels.attribution_text: Yaghan et al. Periductal Mastitis Occurring Among Hubble-Bubble Smokers: A Report of Two Cases and Literature Review.. Cureus 2024. doi:10.7759/cureus.75686. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Periductal mastitis in a patient with history of hubble-bubble smoking This 19-year-old female patient, with a history of daily hubble-bubble smoking presented with a right-sided subareolar mass (double arrows). The diagnosis of periductal mastitis with breast abscess was made. Aspiration revealed thick pus that was evacuated by multiple aspirations (single arrow). The dotted markings were used for the clinical follow up of the response to treatment
in_text_mentions: Aspiration under local anesthesia revealed thick pus (Figure 1). The contents of the abscess were evacuated by multiple aspirations. Gram stain and culture of the aspirate were negative. She received clindamycin 300 mg twice daily for one week. A follow-up in the clinic showed the resolution of her disease. The patient was advised to quit HBS, but she was not compliant with the advice.
